notes: E6 test case dataset. Two state tenants of 500 field workers, eight NGO tenants sharing 500, at day 365. The fourth growth point, added because case 8's curve is the only evidence the exercise produces about scale beyond the pilot, and three points over 180 days is a short baseline. Rolling data means year two accrues at year one's rate, so volume keeps climbing. bundle_path and bundle_revision must be filled in before generating. A tenant may also carry its own bundle_path, which is how H1's 'cover the range of organisation size' is done -- config size drives the syncDetails row count Organisation ids recorded 6 Oct 2026, after provisioning: state-1 and state-2 already existed at 10 and 11, and ngo-1 to ngo-8 were created with the server assigning 12 to 19 -- read back from GET /organisation rather than inferred from the sequence. They held 1-10 before, which named four live organisations; see docs/execution-plan.md. supervisor_level is Taluka, not the TenantSpec default of Sub-Centre: the bundle's hierarchy has no Sub-Centre, and after `from_target_types` truncates at the deepest permitted registration type the chain is State > District > Taluka > Village. Taluka is the tier above a field worker's village, which is what the scenarios mean by supervision one tier up. states-day-180 has carried this since it was built; the pilots inherited the default and would have failed at `cat.plan`.
